project_type: Greenfield full-stack social media web app — Node.js/Express REST API + vanilla HTML/CSS/JS frontend
build_system: npm — no transpiler, no bundler. Files are served statically from public/ by Express. Run: npm install, then npm start (or node server.js). No compile step required.
test_framework: None specified. Manual verification via browser + curl/Postman against the running server on http://localhost:3000
test_command: node server.js (then visit http://localhost:3000 in a browser)
verification_instructions: 1. cd to project root. 2. Run `npm install`. 3. Copy .env.example to .env and set SESSION_SECRET. 4. Run `node server.js`. 5. Open http://localhost:3000 — should redirect to login. 6. Register a new account, log in, create a post, like it, comment, follow another user, check notifications, bookmarks, messages, settings pages all load without JS errors.
snapshot_or_generated_files: uploads/ directory is created at runtime by multer. connect.db SQLite file is auto-created by the database/db.js initializer on first run. Neither should be committed.
environment_constraints: Windows host (PowerShell). Node.js must be installed. SQLite file at database/connect.db is auto-created. The uploads/ folder must exist before multer can write — create it with fs.mkdirSync at server startup. Port defaults to 3000 via process.env.PORT.
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md — greenfield. Follow the spec: no React/Next.js, no mock data, real SQLite persistence, all specified npm packages.
key_patterns: 1. Backend: Express routes in routes/, middleware in middleware/, DB init in database/db.js using better-sqlite3 synchronous API. 2. Frontend: Each page has its own HTML file in public/ and a matching JS file in public/js/. All JS uses Fetch API against /api/* endpoints. CSS variables drive theming — light/dark toggled by adding class 'dark' to <html>. 3. Session auth: express-session with a secret from .env; middleware/auth.js exports requireAuth and optionalAuth. 4. File uploads: multer stores to uploads/, filenames are UUIDs. 5. All API responses are JSON: { success, data, message, error }.
directory_structure: Connect/ — project root. public/ — all frontend files (HTML pages, css/, js/, assets/). routes/ — Express route handlers, one file per resource. middleware/ — auth guard and multer upload config. database/ — db.js (better-sqlite3 init + schema runner) and schema.sql. uploads/ — runtime image storage (not committed). .env — runtime secrets.
